risks.note: Sugarcane crushing declined by 7.51% y-o-y and all three units ceased operations early. The same climatic conditions that lifted sucrose concentration - cool nights, dry weather at maturity, high diurnal temperature variation - constrained vegetative growth and lowered farm yields, so the year was characterised by higher recovery but reduced overall cane productivity. Throughput depends on a biological input the Company does not control.
risks.risk: Cane availability and farm-yield volatility driven by weather

risks.note: Global prices declined by approximately 17% in 2025 with 2026 averages stabilising around ~13-15 cents per pound. Production in major exporting countries outpaced consumption growth, Brazil continues to supply large export volumes, and sentiment remains bearish in the short term with limited near-term catalysts for a sustained recovery. Global production of ~181-190 million tonnes against ~177-178 million tonnes of consumption implies supply comfortably meeting or exceeding demand under most scenarios.
risks.risk: Global sugar oversupply and a sharp price correction

risks.note: Global consumption is growing only ~1-1.5% a year. Rising health awareness is shifting consumers toward low-sugar and sugar-free alternatives over obesity and diabetes concerns, economic slowdown in some regions has moderated purchasing power, and industrial demand in beverages, confectionery and processed foods stays weak - structural shifts in diet preference, not a cyclical dip.
risks.risk: Structurally weak demand growth for sugar

risks.note: Output is a choice between sugar and alcohol from one raw material. In the previous financial year approximately 36.90 lakh quintals of cane crushed were diverted for ethanol production, which impacted recovery levels; in FY 2025-26 the absence of juice diversion is what lifted net recovery to 9.73% from 8% and sugar production to 23.73 lakh quintals, with production sacrifice limited to B-heavy molasses use. Whichever way the diversion decision goes, one revenue stream is given up for the other.
risks.risk: Sugar-versus-ethanol trade-off on the same cane

risks.note: The overall performance of the distillery was adversely impacted by reduced cane crushing operations. A weak cane year transmits directly into the alcohol business through lower molasses feedstock, so the integrated model concentrates rather than diversifies the cane risk.
risks.risk: Distillery earnings tethered to cane crushing volumes

risks.note: The Company operates three sugar mills and two distillery units, all in Uttar Pradesh, with the registered office at Dwarikesh Nagar, Bijnor. A single state's weather, cane pricing policy and crop cycle drive the whole portfolio; there is no geographic hedge across cane-growing regions.
risks.risk: Geographic concentration of the entire asset base in Uttar Pradesh

risks.note: The sugar industry is intrinsically dependent on natural resources and rural ecosystems, which necessitates a measured and responsible approach to business operations. This exposes the Company to water availability, effluent-compliance and agricultural-ecosystem risk in operations involving process heating, distillation and large-volume water use.
risks.risk: Dependence on natural resources and rural ecosystems

risks.note: Sugarcane, the primary raw material, is sourced entirely from local farmers. Cane development, farmer relationships and command-area productivity are therefore the single point of dependence for sugar, cogeneration and distillery output alike, with no alternative feedstock disclosed.
risks.risk: Sole primary raw material sourced entirely from local farmers
